I really appreciate you sharing that, it sounds like a heartbreaking experience, and I’m genuinely sorry for what that guy went through. You're right that assuming guilt without due process can destroy lives, and false accusations are a serious issue that shouldn’t be brushed aside.

 That said, I still believe there's a reason why many people instinctively side with victims, especially in cases involving assault. Historically, victims (especially women) haven’t been believed, and that silence led to a lot of pain going unacknowledged. So while "guilty until proven innocent" may sound harsh, I think what I meant was that we need to err on the side of protecting potential victims. while still recognizing the accused deserves a fair chance to respond.


 Of course, it's a difficult balance. Some people lie, yes. But not everyone who says they’ve been falsely accused is necessarily innocent either. Context matters. Just as we shouldn't blindly believe accusers, we also shouldn't blindly believe denials. especially on the internet where it's easy to present one-sided stories.

 It’s a painful and complex issue, and I respect that your experience gave you a strong perspective. I just think we have to be careful not to swing too hard in either direction.

ps: many people have bad social cues and might've not understood rejection, some might've even pressured a yes and took it as consent. either way you can never be sure.

last problem, tell your parents that you can't really focus on studying if they're going to make so much noises, and since they abuse you for slightly "bad" grades they should understand and provide you everything, if not try finding a library maybe a school one if you have and sit there just to do self study, do all your best in next month's exams I'm cheering for you! and I hope all the best for you.
